items.text: Unified navigation redesign: single data-driven nav replaces per-page hardcoded links across all 17 pages. Desktop top bar with grouped dropdowns (≥641px), hamburger drawer on mobile (≤640px). Nav and footer now sourced from content/settings/nav.json.

"Last Updated" dates now read as a full written date with an ordinal suffix (e.g. "27th June 2026") everywhere they appear on the site, replacing a previous mix of formats. The Model Tracker and Model Directory badges were also corrected to their real last-refresh date.
Reasoning Models node updated to reflect the current generation — Gemini Deep Think and Qwen3's hybrid thinking mode replace older examples.

Our AI cost-collapse article is now "Why AI Prices Have Dropped 200x in Three Years." DeepSeek's real cache-miss input price (US$0.14 per million tokens) meant the original 300x framing overstated the drop, so the numbers and title were corrected.
New search feature — type to find any topic on the map directly.
New sixth root branch, "What Else Matters," with five new topics: AI Agents, MCP (Model Context Protocol), Evaluation & Benchmarks, AI Regulation, and the Cost of AI.
Model Directory expanded from 7 to 10 model cards, and all six major lab cards (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral) refreshed against current releases and pricing (27 June).
Site-wide staleness audit — every page checked and updated so dated claims reflect mid-2026 reality.
Major build-out: the Model Directory, Model Tracker, and Trends hub launched, alongside eight articles and quarterly reports, a restructured navigation, and search-engine and AI-crawler optimisation.
This page launched — every meaningful reader-facing change to the site is now recorded here by date, and a link to it was added to the navigation site-wide.
New Computer Use node added to the Prompting branch — explains how screen-control agents work and what they can and can't do.
New article: AI That Uses Your Computer: What Screen-Control Agents Can and Cannot Do.
New Methodology & Glossary page — explains how rankings, status badges, and cost tiers are worked out, and defines key terms used across the site.

Model Tracker sourcing note corrected — the tracker footer and in-page note previously misattributed rankings to LMSYS Chatbot Arena; replaced with an accurate description of our monthly editorial review process.
Resources page updated — corrected stale facts found during the fortnightly review.
Monthly Model Tracker updated — top models include GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.1 Pro and 9 more.

Model Directory refreshed — the OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Meta Superintelligence Labs, Alibaba and Moonshot cards now reflect current models (GPT-5.6, Claude Sonnet 5, Grok 4.5, Muse Spark 1.1, Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi K3) and corrected availability, replacing stale June content.

Model Directory tidied — every card’s status badge and cost-tier label now uses the site’s documented vocabulary (Market Leader / Highly Competitive / Rising / Disruptor, and Free / Ultra-low / Low / Standard / Premium), so the badges match the Methodology page and the cost row reads evenly.
New article: Before You Trust an AI Agent With Your Accounts.
Resources page updated — corrected stale facts found during the fortnightly review.
New Multimodal Models node added to the Architectures branch.
New article: Voice, Vision, and the End of Text-Only AI.
New article: Running AI on Your Own Computer in 2026: What Actually Works.
Monthly Model Tracker updated — top models include Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 3.1 Pro and 9 more.
Corrected /tracker: added missing Claude Fable 5 row (Anthropic's most capable general-access model, omitted from the Aug 1 run).
New Provenance & Watermarking node added to the What Else Matters branch.
New article: Can You Tell If Something Was Made by AI? The New Labeling Rules, Explained.
New AI Regulation node added to the What Else Matters branch.
New article: The AI Rules Taking Effect in 2026: What You Actually Need to Know.
Resources page updated — corrected stale facts found during the fortnightly review.
